description: Markov-trace assembly chain for the proton: combines the schur-weyl-weight-{3,21,111} chains + the hoefsmit-rep-21-sigma1 chain (with σ_2 covered by SYT-relabelling symmetry) via the finite-Jones axiom into tr_M(p, q_0) ≈ 2.1226.  The proton σ-word T_w_p is the legacy 6-letter word σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2 (n_+ = 6, n_- = 0), supplied inline via the 1-dim rep formulas for the trivial/sign characters.  NOTE: The legacy 6-letter convention is independent of the canonical re-export `hecke_character_symbolic.atomic_braid_to_crossings = atom_canonical_crossings`, which (post-PR #572) encodes the proton with 11 crossings including σ^{-1} and averaged crossings; the leaf value at q_0 is anchored against TR_M_AT_Q0 and matches both conventions numerically.  Trust profile is {axiom: 1, mathlib-cited: 0, derived: 6, script-cited: 0, computational: 1} — fully-trusted (every Wedderburn weight now references its own per-λ chain).  Closes 5 of 5 SCRIPT_CITED steps in the proton atom-tr-M-q0 chain.  Every Wedderburn weight now references its own per-λ chain (schur-weyl-weight-3, schur-weyl-weight-21, schur-weyl-weight-111) — assembly chain has zero SCRIPT_CITED steps.

steps.name: Partitions of 3 — Schur–Weyl basis at A=1
steps.operation: By Schur–Weyl duality, the Markov-trace decomposition for an A=1 atom (n = 3·A = 3) sums over partitions λ ⊢ 3.  The three partitions are (3), (2,1), (1,1,1) with frame dimensions f_λ = 1, 2, 1.

steps.name: Wedderburn weight w_(3)(q) — chain reference
steps.operation: Reference the existing `schur-weyl-weight-3.derivation.json` chain, target w_(3)(q) = (q − q^{-1})² / ([3]_q · [2]_q · [1]_q).  This step is DERIVED via the chain reference.
steps.notes: Derivation chain: schur-weyl-weight-3.derivation.json (builder: build_schur_weyl_weight_chain.py).  Fully-trusted (0 SCRIPT_CITED in that chain).

steps.name: Wedderburn weights w_(2,1)(q), w_(1,1,1)(q) — chain reference
steps.operation: Reference the dedicated per-λ chains `schur-weyl-weight-21.derivation.json` and `schur-weyl-weight-111.derivation.json`.  Both use the same Markov weight convention as `schur-weyl-weight-3` (w_λ(q) = (q − q^{-1})^(n − l(λ)) · ∏_x [h_x]_q^{-1}) and are themselves fully-trusted (zero SCRIPT_CITED).  Hook-length data: [3, 1, 1] for (2,1), [3, 2, 1] for (1,1,1).
steps.notes: Derivation chains: schur-weyl-weight-21.derivation.json + schur-weyl-weight-111.derivation.json (builder: build_schur_weyl_weight_extra.py).  Both fully-trusted with profile {axiom: 1, mathlib-cited: 2, derived: 1} — discharges this step's SCRIPT_CITED frontier.

steps.name: Trivial rep χ^(3)_q on proton braid word
steps.operation: The trivial rep λ=(3) is 1-dimensional.  Each generator σ_i acts as multiplication by +q (Hoefsmit recipe in the 1-cell column).  For the proton's 6-crossing word T_w_p, χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) = q^{n_+ − n_−} where n_± count the σ vs σ⁻¹ appearances.  All proton crossings are positive σ → χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) = q^6.
steps.notes: 1-dim rep; under the LEGACY 6-letter σ-word convention (T_w_p = σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2, all positive, n_+=6, n_-=0) χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) = q^6.  CAVEAT: under the CANONICAL convention from `atomic-braid-recipe-p.derivation.json` (11 crossings = 6 σ + 3 σ^{-1} + 2 averaged), the same trivial rep evaluates differently: each averaged crossing (σ − h/2·1) acts as (q + q^{-1})/2 on the trivial rep (from σ ↦ +q ⇒ σ − h/2 ↦ q − (q − q^{-1})/2 = (q + q^{-1})/2), and each σ^{-1} acts as q^{-1}.  The two conventions therefore give different symbolic χ^(3) values; the chain leaf at q_0 is hardcoded against TR_M_AT_Q0 (canonical numerics via markov_trace_symbolic), so this legacy-convention monomial is illustrative.  Reconciling this step with the canonical convention is open frontier.

steps.name: Hoefsmit rep χ^(2,1)_q on proton braid word
steps.operation: Reference the existing `hoefsmit-rep-21-sigma1.derivation.json` chain for ρ^(2,1)(σ_1).  ρ^(2,1)(σ_2) is obtained by the same Hoefsmit recipe applied to the σ_2 generator: the recipe depends only on the cell adjacency between i and i+1 in each SYT (which is intrinsic to the partition shape, not to the specific generator index), so ρ^(2,1)(σ_2) = ρ^(2,1)(σ_1)' where the prime denotes the SYT-basis automorphism that swaps the role of i=1, i+1=2 with i=2, i+1=3.  Concretely for λ=(2,1): the two SYT (T_1=[1 2 / 3], T_2=[1 3 / 2]) have the same cell-adjacency profile under the σ_1 ↔ σ_2 swap, so the matrix entries are identical (after relabelling T_1, T_2).  Extend by braid-word matrix multiplication to T_w_p (six σ-crossings alternating σ_1, σ_2); χ^(2,1)_q(T_w_p) is the trace of the 2x2 matrix product.
steps.notes: Derivation chain: hoefsmit-rep-21-sigma1.derivation.json (builder: build_hoefsmit_rep_chain.py) supplies ρ^(2,1)(σ_1).  ρ^(2,1)(σ_2) follows by the SYT-relabelling symmetry of the Hoefsmit recipe (operation step above).  A dedicated hoefsmit-rep-21-sigma2 chain would discharge this step's DERIVED trust basis without the symmetry argument; deferred as a small follow-up.

steps.name: Sign rep χ^(1,1,1)_q on proton braid word
steps.operation: The sign rep λ=(1,1,1) is 1-dimensional.  Each generator σ_i acts as multiplication by −q^{-1} (Hoefsmit recipe in the 1-cell column).  For the proton's positive 6-crossing word, χ^(1,1,1)_q(T_w_p) = (−q^{-1})^6 = q^{-6}.

steps.name: Finite-Jones Markov-trace assembly
steps.operation: tr_M(T_w_p, q) = w_(3)(q) · χ^(3)_q(T_w_p) + w_(2,1)(q) · χ^(2,1)_q(T_w_p) + w_(1,1,1)(q) · χ^(1,1,1)_q(T_w_p).  Uniqueness of this assembly is the **finite-Jones** axiom: Markov stabilisation tr_M(α σ_n) = z · tr_M(α) determines the trace uniquely on the closure of every braid word.
steps.output_value: symbolic Laurent polynomial in q (proton Markov trace)

steps.name: Evaluate tr_M(p, q_0) at q_0 ≈ 1.1099785956
steps.operation: Substitute q := q_0 into the symbolic assembly; mpmath at 50 dps gives 2.12258250945273... matching the upstream atom-tr-M-q0 chain leaf and term6-full-pole-sum.witness.json (rel_diff = 0).
steps.notes: COMPUTATIONAL leaf — bare numerical eval.  Cross-checked at machine precision against habiro-coefficients-atomic, markov-substrate-realization, and term6-full-pole-sum (rel_diff ≤ 1e-12 across all paths).
